questions.text: A health insurance plan that reimburses actual hospital bills is an example of:
questions.explanation: Reimbursement-based health policies are indemnity-based, as they compensate for actual expenses incurred.

questions.text: Utmost good faith (Uberrimae Fidei) requires:
options: Insurer to disclose all underwriting details to insured
Both parties to disclose all material facts truthfully
Insured to pay premium before policy issuance
questions.explanation: Both insurer and insured must act with complete honesty and disclose all material facts before the contract.

questions.text: Combining investment and insurance often results in:
options: Higher risk cover and lower premium
Lower risk cover and higher premium
questions.explanation: When insurance and investment are combined, adequate cover often becomes unaffordable, compromising protection.

questions.text: Which type of need does health insurance primarily address?
options: Income protection from unexpected medical expenses
questions.explanation: Health insurance protects income from being eroded by sudden and high medical costs.

questions.text: Portability in health insurance means:
options: Ability to switch insurers without losing policy benefits
Policy can be transferred to another person
Policy can be converted to life insurance
questions.explanation: Portability allows policyholders to switch insurers while retaining accumulated benefits and waiting periods.

questions.text: Term insurance provides:
questions.explanation: Term insurance is pure risk cover providing death benefit only, without any investment component.

questions.text: A term plan with return of premium is:
options: Costlier than pure term plan and includes refund of premiums
Same cost as pure term plan
questions.explanation: Term with return of premium costs more, as extra premium is invested to refund on maturity.

questions.text: Which concept represents the present value of future income available to dependents?
questions.explanation: Human Life Value (HLV) is the present value of future income expected to support dependents.

questions.text: Which of the following is an advantage of ULIPs over mutual funds?
options: Free fund switches between asset classes without tax implications
questions.explanation: ULIPs allow fund switches within the same insurer without incurring tax or exit load.

questions.text: Group life insurance offers:
options: Cheaper coverage for employees as a group
questions.explanation: Group life insurance provides lower-cost coverage collectively to employees or organization members.

questions.text: Which of the following risks is LEAST suited for general (non-life) insurance?
options: Normal wear and tear of machinery
questions.explanation: Normal wear and tear is expected and gradual, not uncertain or fortuitous, so it is typically excluded.

questions.text: Insurance web aggregators typically:
options: Sell only their own insurance products
Provide online comparison of policies from multiple insurers
Issue policies on behalf of IRDAI
questions.explanation: Web aggregators host comparison platforms and often facilitate online purchase from several insurance companies.

questions.text: Fidelity insurance is generally taken to cover:
options: Losses from employee fraud, forgery or dishonesty
questions.explanation: Fidelity insurance protects employers against financial losses due to dishonest acts by employees.

questions.text: A family floater health policy:
options: Provides separate sum insured for each member
Shares a single sum insured among all covered family members
Can only cover parents and in-laws
Is available only to senior citizens
questions.explanation: In a family floater, the sum insured is common and can be used by any covered family member.

questions.text: Liability insurance primarily covers:
options: Loss of or damage to own assets
Legal liability to third parties for injury or property damage
questions.explanation: Liability insurance indemnifies the insured for damages payable under law to third parties.

questions.text: If actual returns are lower than projected during retirement, the investor should ideally:
questions.explanation: Adjusting withdrawals or spending ensures the corpus lasts longer if returns underperform.

questions.text: The main objective of the accumulation phase is to:
options: Build the required corpus through systematic investment
questions.explanation: The accumulation phase focuses on disciplined saving and investing to build the desired retirement corpus.

questions.text: Corpus longevity refers to:
options: The expected life of investments post-retirement
Number of years the corpus will sustain withdrawals
Average age at death in a population
Return rate of fixed income securities
questions.explanation: Corpus longevity means how long the retirement fund lasts when withdrawals begin.

questions.text: Which factor most directly increases the corpus needed for retirement?
options: Higher expected inflation during and before retirement
questions.explanation: Higher inflation raises the future cost of living and therefore increases the corpus needed to fund retirement expenses.

questions.text: A diversified retirement corpus should include:
options: A mix of growth, income, and liquid assets
questions.explanation: Diversification across asset types helps balance growth, income, and liquidity needs.

questions.text: Which stage of retirement is associated with building assets, family responsibilities and recognising the impact of ageing?
questions.explanation: The preparation stage covers working years when people handle goals like housing, children’s education and insurance while saving for retirement.

questions.text: The maximum tax-free gratuity limit under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 is:
questions.explanation: The maximum tax-free gratuity amount is ₹20 lakh.

questions.text: At maturity, a minimum of what percentage of NPS corpus must be used to buy an annuity?
questions.explanation: 40% of the NPS corpus must be used to purchase an annuity at retirement.

questions.text: Maximum investment under POMIS for single account holder is:
questions.explanation: The maximum investment permitted under POMIS is ₹15 lakh.

questions.text: Liquidity in a retirement portfolio is essential to handle:
questions.explanation: Liquidity helps meet unexpected expenses without disturbing income assets.

questions.text: Maximum investment allowed in PMVVY per senior citizen is:
questions.explanation: PMVVY permits up to ₹15 lakh per senior citizen.

questions.text: Public Provident Fund (PPF) has a lock-in period of:
questions.explanation: PPF has a maturity of 15 years, extendable in 5-year blocks.

questions.text: Under the Universal Account Number (UAN) system, an employee can:
options: Transfer and track all EPF accounts under a single identifier
Invest in equity mutual funds directly
questions.explanation: UAN provides a unique identifier to track and transfer EPF accounts across employers.

questions.text: The primary role of an investment adviser in retirement planning is to:
options: Understand client goals and design strategies for steady post-retirement income
File tax returns on behalf of the client
questions.explanation: An investment adviser aligns client goals, risk tolerance, and timelines to ensure steady and sustainable post-retirement income.

questions.text: Which risk arises if a person withdraws EPF funds early before retirement?
options: Shortfall risk due to loss of compounding
questions.explanation: Premature withdrawals break compounding and reduce the corpus available for retirement.

questions.text: A good adviser should recommend withdrawal rates that:
options: Are sustainable over the retiree’s lifetime
questions.explanation: Withdrawal rates should ensure that the corpus lasts for the entire expected lifetime of the retiree.

questions.text: In the pre-retirement phase, the focus should be on products that:
options: Generate fixed income with low growth
Allow growth through market participation despite some risk
questions.explanation: During accumulation, higher risk tolerance allows for equity or market-linked growth products.

questions.text: Which Excel function helps estimate retirement corpus required?
questions.explanation: The PV (Present Value) function is used to estimate the corpus required to meet future retirement expenses.

questions.text: Long-term capital losses can be set off against:
questions.explanation: Long-term capital losses can only be set off against long-term capital gains.

questions.text: Which of these is a correct example of EET investment?
questions.explanation: ELSS investments are EET — tax-deductible on investment, returns taxed on withdrawal.

questions.text: Under the new regime (post July 2024), short-term capital gains under Section 111A are taxed at:
questions.explanation: Finance Act, 2024 raised the tax rate on short-term capital gains covered under Section 111A to 20%.

questions.text: Conversion of gold into Electronic Gold Receipt (EGR) is:
options: Not a transfer under the Act
questions.explanation: Conversion of gold into Electronic Gold Receipt (EGR) and vice versa is not treated as a transfer under Section 47.

questions.text: Which of these incomes is specifically included under 'Income from Other Sources'?
options: Winnings from lotteries or online games
questions.explanation: Winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, and online games are always taxed under 'Income from Other Sources'.

questions.text: Buyback proceeds received by shareholders are taxed as dividend from which date?
questions.explanation: From 1 October 2024, buyback proceeds are taxable as dividend under 'Income from Other Sources'.

questions.text: Under Chapter XII-A, long-term capital gains for NRIs are taxed at:
questions.explanation: NRIs opting for Chapter XII-A are taxed at 12.5% on long-term capital gains from eligible investments.

questions.text: Interest income from debt instruments is taxable under which head if not part of business income?
questions.explanation: Interest income from debt instruments is taxed under 'Income from Other Sources' unless held as business income.

questions.text: Long-term capital gain exemption limit for residents under Section 112A is:
questions.explanation: The Finance Act 2024 increased the LTCG exemption threshold under Section 112A to ₹1.25 lakh.

questions.text: Section 87A rebate is not available against tax on:
questions.explanation: Rebate under Section 87A cannot be used to offset tax on LTCG under Section 112A.

questions.text: Category-I and II AIFs enjoy pass-through status for which type of income?
questions.explanation: Pass-through applies to capital gains and other income, not to business income, which is taxed at AIF level.

questions.text: Stock Lending and Borrowing in India is governed by:
questions.explanation: SLB transactions are governed by SEBI’s Securities Lending Scheme, 1997.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is true about a 'Registered Will'?
options: It provides stronger evidence of authenticity
It must be registered within 30 days
questions.explanation: A registered will is not mandatory but provides stronger legal proof of validity.

questions.text: Which of the following best defines 'Gross Estate'?
options: All real and personal properties owned
questions.explanation: Gross Estate includes all real, personal, and financial assets that determine one’s net worth.

questions.text: Estate taxes in India are:
questions.explanation: Estate duty was abolished in 1985; inheritance is currently tax-free in India.

questions.text: Who is eligible to be appointed as a legal guardian for minors?
options: Court-appointed person or as specified in a Will
questions.explanation: Guardians are either court-appointed or designated under a valid will for minor dependents.

questions.text: Under Hindu Succession Act, ancestral property passes to legal heirs through:
questions.explanation: Ancestral property devolves through the Hindu coparcenary system automatically.

questions.text: What is a 'Will'?
options: A legal declaration of a person’s intent regarding property distribution after death
A transfer deed executed during lifetime
questions.explanation: A will is a legal document specifying how assets should be distributed after death.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT true about a Gift?
options: It is made voluntarily and without consideration
It is taxable unless exempted by law
It must be accepted by the donee
questions.explanation: A gift cannot be revoked unilaterally unless both parties agree or specific conditions exist.

questions.text: Who is the person appointed to administer a Will?
questions.explanation: An executor is responsible for administering the estate as per the Will.

questions.text: A trust created for charitable purposes is regulated by:
options: Public Trusts Act of the respective state
questions.explanation: Charitable trusts are governed by state-specific Public Trust Acts.

questions.text: Who among the following can be appointed as a trustee?
questions.explanation: A trustee can be an individual or corporate entity capable of managing assets.

questions.text: Which type of Power of Attorney provides broad powers?
questions.explanation: General POA provides wide-ranging powers to act on behalf of the principal.

questions.text: Who grants a probate of a Will?
questions.explanation: Probate is granted by a competent District Court as per Indian Succession Act.

questions.text: Who introduced the concept of Bounded Rationality?
questions.explanation: Herbert Simon proposed Bounded Rationality, explaining how limited information leads to satisficing decisions.

questions.text: Mental Accounting Bias leads investors to:
options: Treat identical sums differently based on their source or purpose
questions.explanation: Mental Accounting involves irrational categorization of money, such as treating bonuses differently from salary.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT a behavioural explanation for market anomalies?
questions.explanation: The Efficient Market Hypothesis assumes rationality and does not explain anomalies.

questions.text: The best way to counter buying insurance just for tax saving is to:
options: Compare returns of term plan plus investment with endowment plans
questions.explanation: Advisers should show that term insurance plus proper investment usually outperforms endowment plans.

questions.text: Investment advisers can manage emotional clients by:
options: Providing objective data and rational alternatives
questions.explanation: Objective, fact-based counselling helps clients take rational decisions even under emotional stress.

questions.text: The key emotional cycle most investors face is between:
questions.explanation: Greed and fear dominate investor psychology, driving irrational market moves.

questions.text: A valid risk profiling questionnaire should be:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates that questionnaires should be simple, objective, and unbiased to ensure reliability.

questions.text: Diversification works best when asset classes have:
questions.explanation: Low or negative correlation among asset classes ensures smoother portfolio performance.

questions.text: Tactical Asset Allocation refers to:
options: Adjusting asset mix based on expected market behaviour
Maintaining static portfolios for long-term goals
questions.explanation: Tactical allocation uses market forecasts to temporarily change asset weights for potential gain.

questions.text: Which of the following factors increases risk appetite?
questions.explanation: With more earning members, income stability improves, leading to higher risk tolerance.

questions.text: A model portfolio helps advisers by:
options: Providing identical portfolios to all clients
Customizing recommendations based on client profile
questions.explanation: Model portfolios act as templates that can be customized based on each client’s unique circumstances.

questions.text: SEBI requires that a client’s risk profile must be:
options: Updated periodically or after major life changes
questions.explanation: Regulations mandate regular review, especially after life or financial changes, to ensure suitability.

questions.text: Which SEBI regulation mandates risk profiling by investment advisers?
questions.explanation: Regulation 16 of SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 mandates risk profiling to ensure product suitability.

questions.text: Which of the following describes a conservative investor?
options: Prefers low risk and steady returns
Willing to take high risk for short-term gains
questions.explanation: Conservative investors prioritize capital protection and stable income over high returns.

questions.text: Aggressive investors are most likely to:
options: Take active exposure to equities and growth assets
questions.explanation: Aggressive investors are experienced and willing to accept higher volatility for long-term gains.

questions.text: What is the primary limitation of self-assessment risk profiling tools?
options: Investors may guess socially desirable answers
questions.explanation: Investors may attempt to 'guess' the right answers instead of responding truthfully, reducing accuracy.

questions.text: An investor near retirement should ideally have:
options: Balanced mix with higher debt allocation
questions.explanation: Retirees prioritize safety and income stability, so debt-heavy portfolios suit them better.

questions.text: Risk profiling primarily helps an investment adviser to:
options: Determine the client’s ability and willingness to take risk
questions.explanation: Risk profiling helps determine both the financial ability and psychological willingness of a client to take investment risk.

questions.text: Which personality trait is most associated with high risk-taking ability?
questions.explanation: Daring and adventurous individuals are psychologically more open to investment risks.

questions.text: Asset allocation primarily aims to:
questions.explanation: Asset allocation spreads risk across asset classes to stabilize returns and minimize loss exposure.

questions.text: REITs primarily invest in:
options: Infrastructure projects like bridges and roads
Commercial real estate generating rental income
questions.explanation: REITs (Real Estate Investment Trusts) mainly invest in income-generating commercial properties.

questions.text: Between Company Deposits and Debentures, which is riskier?
questions.explanation: Company deposits are unsecured, whereas debentures are usually secured; hence deposits carry higher risk.

questions.text: Mutual Funds are regulated by ______, while ULIPs are regulated by ______.
questions.explanation: Mutual funds fall under SEBI, while ULIPs are under the jurisdiction of IRDAI.

questions.text: Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) differ from Index Funds because:
options: They are sold only by AMCs
They are traded on stock exchanges like shares
They are only available for debt instruments
questions.explanation: ETFs are listed and traded on exchanges, unlike index funds which are transacted at NAV with AMCs.

questions.text: In National Pension System (NPS) Tier 1, what percentage of corpus can be withdrawn tax-free at age 60?
questions.explanation: At retirement, 60% of NPS corpus can be withdrawn tax-free; 40% must be used to buy an annuity.

questions.text: Which of the following investment types carries the highest diversification benefit?
questions.explanation: Mutual funds pool investors’ money into diversified portfolios, reducing risk concentration.

questions.text: Minimum investment amount for a Portfolio Management Service (PMS) is:
questions.explanation: As per SEBI norms, the minimum investment in PMS is ₹50 lakh.

questions.text: ULIPs issued after February 1, 2021 lose Section 10(10D) exemption if annual premium exceeds:
questions.explanation: ULIPs with premiums above ₹2.5 lakh per year no longer qualify for tax exemption under Section 10(10D).

questions.text: In comparison of debt instruments, liquidity is highest in:
questions.explanation: Bank FDs offer instant liquidity, albeit with penalties for premature withdrawal.

questions.text: Which form of gold investment does NOT attract GST?
questions.explanation: Sovereign Gold Bonds are paper-based and exempt from GST.

questions.text: Which of the following is a SEBI-mandated product that must disclose performance data publicly?
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates performance disclosure for Mutual Funds and Portfolio Management Services.

questions.text: Category III Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) require a minimum investment of:
questions.explanation: AIF Category III has a minimum entry threshold of ₹1 crore per investor.

questions.text: What is the lock-in period for investments in PPF?
questions.explanation: PPF has a lock-in of 15 years, with partial withdrawals allowed after 5 years.

questions.case_text: An employee, Lalit, has the option between leaving his retirement money in the company’s provident fund at 8% p.a. or transferring it to a pension product that offers 6% guaranteed plus a possible bonus. He is 52 and plans to retire at 60. He is confused about which option better suits his retirement planning.

questions.text: Which of the following is TRUE about provident fund balances?
options: They usually offer tax-efficient, relatively stable returns
They are extremely volatile like equity
They cannot be used for retirement
They always give lower returns than savings accounts
questions.explanation: Provident funds are generally debt-oriented, offer relatively stable returns and often enjoy tax advantages.

questions.text: What is the PRIMARY advantage of shifting to a pension product?
options: Guaranteed annuity and structured retirement income
No need to plan for retirement
questions.explanation: Pension products convert accumulated corpus into organized retirement income, though typically with lower liquidity.

questions.text: Which factor should Lalit examine carefully in the pension product?
questions.explanation: Key aspects include surrender terms, vesting age, annuity options, charges and effective yield to decide suitability.

questions.text: From a risk perspective, keeping funds in provident fund until retirement is:
questions.explanation: Provident funds invest mainly in fixed income and some equity as per regulation, so volatility is much lower than pure equity.

questions.text: Which is a prudent strategy for Lalit?
options: Decide purely based on friends’ advice
Evaluate both options’ effective post-tax returns, liquidity and suitability to his retirement income needs
Switch entirely based on highest commission product
questions.explanation: Comparing post-tax returns, flexibility, charges, and how each product fits his retirement income plan is the correct approach.

questions.case_text: Deepak, 35, wants to retire at 60. His current monthly expenses are ₹60,000. He expects inflation at 6% p.a. and post-retirement portfolio return at 8% p.a. He wants to provide for 25 years in retirement. He currently has no separate retirement corpus but can invest ₹25,000 per month towards retirement.

questions.text: What is Deepak’s CURRENT annual expense level?
questions.explanation: Annual expenses = 60,000 × 12 = ₹7,20,000? However exam-style rounding may treat 60,000 × 12 as 7.2 lakh, but the option closest to typical demonstration is ₹7,20,000. (Use the option that matches 60,000 × 12).

questions.text: Roughly how many years are left for his retirement planning?
questions.explanation: Deepak is 35 and wants to retire at 60, so he has 25 years to accumulate his retirement corpus.

questions.text: If inflation is 6%, his annual expenses at retirement (start of age 60) will be approximately how many times today’s expenses?
questions.explanation: Over 25 years at 6%, (1.06)^25 is roughly 4.29; however exam-style approximations often round this closer to 4x. Students are expected to recognize that expenses more than triple or quadruple due to inflation.

questions.text: Which of the following is the BEST way to estimate the retirement corpus required?
options: Taking current income and multiplying by 5
Inflating expenses to retirement and then discounting over retirement years at real rate
Ignoring inflation and using current expenses
questions.explanation: Proper retirement planning inflates current expenses to retirement date and then discounts over the retirement period using real return (post-inflation).

questions.text: What type of asset allocation is MOST suitable for Deepak during his accumulation phase?
questions.explanation: With a 25-year horizon, growth assets like equity should dominate the portfolio, supported by some debt for stability.

questions.case_text: Mr. Deshmukh, 58, remarried after the death of his first wife. He has a son from his first marriage and a daughter from his second marriage. He owns a house, mutual funds and a small business. He wants to ensure that his current spouse and both children are taken care of without disputes after his death, especially since the son and stepmother do not get along well.

questions.text: In a blended family situation like this, which estate planning tool is MOST important to avoid ambiguity?
questions.explanation: A clear Will specifying how assets are to be divided among spouse and children helps reduce uncertainty and potential conflict in blended families.

questions.text: Why might a TRUST be considered in this case?
options: To hold assets for the benefit of spouse and children with rules on timing and conditions of distribution
questions.explanation: A private trust can provide structured distribution (e.g., income to spouse for life, corpus to children later), protect against mismanagement and ensure long-term continuity according to the settlor’s wishes.

questions.text: What role can life insurance play in such blended family estate planning?
options: Create a separate corpus earmarked for one branch of the family to balance inheritances
questions.explanation: Life insurance can be used to create an additional pool of funds so that, for example, the spouse can retain the house while the child from the first marriage receives a fair share via policy proceeds, reducing conflict.

questions.text: Why is it especially important for Deshmukh to COMMUNICATE his plan to family members?
options: To minimize surprises and resentment, though they cannot dictate his decisions
questions.explanation: While he has freedom to distribute his estate, explaining the rationale may reduce emotional friction and build understanding among beneficiaries.

questions.text: From a planner’s perspective, the KEY objective in this case is to:
options: Ensure fair and practical distribution considering emotional dynamics, legal rules and financial security of all dependents
questions.explanation: Estate planning must combine technical considerations with sensitivity to family relationships, aiming for fairness, clarity and security for all dependents.

questions.case_text: Rajesh, 62, holds a demat account and mutual funds where his wife is the nominee. He has drafted a Will that leaves his entire share portfolio equally to both his son and daughter, but he has not updated the nominations. His son thinks that as nominee in some accounts he will automatically become owner and is worried that his sister may contest.

questions.text: In general, NOMINATION in financial assets ensures:
options: Only a mechanism for the institution to release funds to nominee, subject to rights of legal heirs
That legal heirs lose their rights
questions.explanation: Nomination is a facility for quick transfer of assets to the nominee, who often acts as a trustee for the legal heirs. The ultimate ownership is determined by succession laws and the Will, not by nomination alone.

questions.text: If Rajesh’s valid Will states that shares are to be shared EQUALLY between son and daughter, but nomination is only in favour of son, which usually prevails for beneficial ownership?
options: Will, subject to probate/validation, generally determines beneficial ownership
questions.explanation: The Will expresses Rajesh’s intention about distribution of his estate. The nominee receives the securities procedurally, but must honour the bequests in the Will, subject to legal process and personal succession law.

questions.text: What is a prudent action for Rajesh to reduce possible disputes?
options: Keep Will secret and conflicting with nominations
Align nominations with intended beneficiaries or clearly explain in the Will and to children
Transfer all assets only to one child without communication
questions.explanation: Either aligning nominations with the Will or clearly documenting and communicating the rationale helps prevent misunderstandings and reduces the risk of litigation between heirs.

questions.text: Why is it important for Rajesh to INFORM his family about the contents of his Will?
options: To reduce surprise, build understanding, and prevent conflicts after his death
To obtain their signatures of approval
It is never advisable to inform
questions.explanation: Explaining his intentions during his lifetime can help manage expectations and avoid disputes. However, children cannot override his freedom to make a Will; communication simply improves transparency.

questions.text: From an estate planning perspective, Rajesh’s adviser should recommend:
options: Relying solely on nominations without a Will
Ensuring he has a clear, updated Will, proper nominations, and documented communication with heirs
Transferring all assets to nominees immediately
questions.explanation: A coherent estate plan uses both Will and nominations in a consistent manner, with proper documentation and some communication, to ensure smooth transfer and minimal conflict.

questions.case_text: A young couple, Nikhil (30) and Asha (28), approach an investment adviser. Their goals are: build emergency fund in 1 year, buy a house in 7 years, and plan for retirement at 60. Their combined income is ₹1.5 lakh per month with expenses of ₹90,000. They have no significant assets yet.

questions.text: What is their MONTHLY SURPLUS available for goals, approximately?
questions.explanation: Surplus ≈ 1.5 lakh – 90,000 = ₹60,000; depending on allowances for contingencies, the closest option could be ₹60,000.

questions.text: Which goal should be prioritized FIRST?
questions.explanation: Emergency fund is the foundation; without it, other goals can be derailed by unexpected events.

questions.text: What kind of product is MOST suitable for the emergency fund?
questions.explanation: Emergency funds require high liquidity and low risk, making liquid funds or savings accounts appropriate.

questions.text: For the 7-year house purchase goal, which asset allocation is MORE appropriate?
questions.explanation: A medium-term goal can use a blend of growth (equity) and stability (debt) rather than extreme allocations.

questions.text: For retirement at 60, their plan should focus on:
options: Long-term equity-oriented investments and periodic review
questions.explanation: Long-term goals like retirement benefit from equity-oriented investments with regular review and rebalancing.

questions.case_text: Anita, 50, has a family floater health policy of ₹5 lakh and no critical illness cover. She is worried about high treatment costs in case of cancer or heart disease. She wants to know whether critical illness insurance is necessary when she already has a regular health policy.

questions.text: How does a CRITICAL ILLNESS policy generally pay benefits?
options: Pays a lump sum on diagnosis of listed illness
questions.explanation: Critical illness plans pay a lump sum amount on first diagnosis of specified illnesses, irrespective of the actual hospitalization cost.

questions.text: Why might Anita need critical illness insurance despite having health insurance?
options: Health insurance does not cover surgery
Health insurance always has co-pay only
Critical illness cover can fund income loss and non-medical expenses
Critical illness policies are cheaper than all other covers
questions.explanation: Lump sum from critical illness cover can be used for income replacement, travel, special diet and other non-medical expenses that regular health policies don’t reimburse.

questions.text: Which factor is MOST important while choosing a critical illness policy?
options: Number of illnesses and clear definitions
questions.explanation: The scope of coverage, precise definitions and waiting periods for illnesses are crucial to assess the usefulness of the policy.

questions.text: At age 50, which of the following is TRUE regarding buying new health and critical illness cover?
options: Possibility of exclusions or loading is higher
Insurers must accept every proposal without conditions
questions.explanation: At higher ages, insurers may impose waiting periods, exclusions or loadings and may insist on medical underwriting.

questions.text: What is a prudent strategy for Anita?
options: Buy an adequate term plan, top up health cover, and add critical illness cover
Surrender health insurance and buy only critical illness
Avoid insurance and invest all in equity
questions.explanation: An integrated risk plan with life, health, and critical illness insurance reduces the financial impact of serious health events.
